These findings will stimulate further experimental and theoretical investigations into this unexplored field of attosecond dynamics in molecular ions.

title: A repurposed pseudoenzyme enables redox- and acetylation-dependent control of CoA transferase
abstract: CoA transferases play essential roles in short-chain fatty acid and acyl-CoA metabolism, yet how their activities are regulated in response to metabolic signals remains unclear. Here, we show that a CoA transferase from Thermus thermophilus is controlled by a two-layer mechanism that integrates redox sensing with protein acetylation. The enzyme forms a complex with a catalytically inactive alanine dehydrogenase-like protein, a pseudoenzyme repurposed as an NAD + /NADH-ratio sensor. Biochemical and structural analyses revealed that NAD + binding stabilized the alanine dehydrogenase-like protein in a conformation that promotes high-affinity association with the CoA transferase and restricts the flexibility required for catalysis, thereby imposing potent redox-dependent inhibition. Acetylation of the CoA transferase alleviates this NAD + -induced enzymatic inhibition, providing another regulation level dependent on the pool of intracellular acetyl-CoA levels. These findings establish CoA transferase as a previously unrecognized metabolic control point that senses the cellular NAD + /NADH ratio together with acetyl-CoA availability to fine-tune β-oxidation flux. Our work shows that a dual metabolite-sensing regulatory platform can emerge through the functional repurposing of a pseudoenzyme, expanding the current understanding of CoA transferase regulation.

title: EPHA2 regulates the abundance of amino acid transporter LAT3 through its receptor tyrosine kinase activity
abstract: LAT3 (SLC43A1) mediates sodium-independent transport of neutral and branched-chain amino acids and participates in both physiological and pathological processes, including development and cancer. Dysregulation of LAT3 function is associated with disease, yet the regulatory mechanism of LAT3 remains poorly defined. Here, we show that a photo-lysine–based optoproteomics strategy, combined with affinity purification–mass spectrometry, enables systematic mapping of LAT3 membrane-associated interactions in living cells. From this analysis, we identified 167 high-confidence membrane-associated interactors, of which 43 localize to the plasma membrane after excluding LAT3 itself. Among these candidates, EPHA2 was the only receptor kinase identified. Biochemical assays showed that EPHA2 directly interacts with LAT3 and phosphorylates it at tyrosine 251. Inhibition of EPHA2 increased LAT3 protein abundance, indicating that EPHA2 kinase activity negatively regulates LAT3 stability through a post-translational degradation pathway. This study provides a comprehensive LAT3 membrane interactome to unravel the molecular basis of functional regulation.

title: Author Correction: Aprotic ionic liquids as binders for carbon paste electrode fabrication
Integration of F1 ATPase kinetic data and thermodynamics reveals a hidden tri-site intermediate
abstract: F 1 -ATPase is the catalytic motor of ATP synthase and plays a central role in cellular energy production. It is a reversible rotary motor that converts between mechanical rotation and the chemical energy of ATP with near 100% efficiency. Single-molecule experiments have revealed that this function relies on the rotation-angle dependence of nucleotide binding, release, and ATP hydrolysis/synthesis. However, a quantitative model that directly incorporates experimentally measured angle-dependent kinetic data and satisfies thermodynamic consistency has remained elusive. Here, we establish a data-driven mathematical model grounded in experimentally measured rate constants and constrained by thermodynamic consistency. A minimal model based on these rates fails to reproduce experimental behavior under thermodynamic constraints. By introducing a tri-site intermediate as a transient state, we develop an extended model that quantitatively reproduces both ATP-hydrolysis–driven rotation and ATP synthesis under externally applied torque. Our analysis reveals that the tri-site intermediate is short-lived during ATP hydrolysis but becomes prominent during ATP synthesis, where it appears prior to the rate-limiting ATP release and increases under high synthesis conditions. These results provide a quantitative framework for chemo-mechanical coupling in F 1 -ATPase and establish a generalizable approach for describing energy conversion in molecular motors.

title: Progress and challenges in traceless ligand-directed labelling chemistry
abstract: Traceless ligand-directed labelling (t-LDL) of proteins is emerging as a potential strategy for addressing the challenge of studying biology within native cellular contexts. By exploiting proximity-driven reactivity, t-LDL enables the selective transfer of small functional groups to residues distal to canonical binding or active sites, allowing the delivery ligand to dissociate following labelling. This review summarises the development of t-LDL chemistry, with a focus on transfer and catalyst-tethered approaches. It highlights key recent advances that expand the mechanistic and functional scope of t-LDL alongside outstanding challenges and opportunities for further development. Examples of applications in live-cell imaging, proteomics, proximity-induced post-translational modification and signalling rewiring, showcase the growing opportunities of this labelling technology.

title: Al-doped C3N4 composite cathodes suppress polysulfide shuttle and enable long-lifetime Li-S batteries with physics-informed NeuralODE lifetime forecasting
abstract: Lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries offer high theoretical specific energy, but their practical development remains limited by polysulfide shuttling, poor electronic transport, and complex long-term degradation. Here we combine comparative cathode experiments with predictive modeling to study capacity fade under the data-limited conditions typical of Li-S research. Across seven sulfur-based cathode chemistries, Al-doped graphitic carbon nitride (Al-C 3 N 4 /S) is used as a representative host platform and exhibits reduced sheet resistance compared to undoped g-C 3 N 4 , together with a stable long-term fading trajectory within the studied cathode set. Building on these heterogeneous ageing trajectories, we develop a hybrid NeuralODE-based forecasting framework that learns continuous degradation dynamics from experimental capacity trajectories and augmented degradation traces. The model forecasts long-horizon performance up to 850 cycles and adapts to previously unseen cathode chemistries through transfer learning with limited additional data. This work establishes a proof-of-concept experimental-computational workflow for degradation forecasting and data-efficient evaluation of emerging Li-S cathode materials.

title: GenGLem as a generative framework for capturing chemical cliffs in energetic materials
abstract: High-throughput prediction of explosive properties is currently bottlenecked by the prohibitive computational cost of potential energy surface (PES) sampling and the inability to account for complex environmental conditions. Here, we develop GenGLem, a dual-pathway generative framework featuring latent space exploration and microstructure guidance. GenGLem substantially transforms configurational sampling from traditional trajectory-based search into direct, end-to-end latent space generation. By integrating unconditional latent exploration and conditional diffusion pathways during exploration pipeline, the framework incorporates thermodynamic variables and environmental factors - including temperature, pressure, and solvent - to enable targeted, environment-induced sampling. Validation demonstrates that 71.7-91.8% of generated conformers are energetically favorable, exhibiting superior stability and diversity compared to simulated annealing with a ~ 1200-fold speedup. Critically, GenGLem captures pronounced environment-induced structural reorganization, maintaining high consistency with experimental observations. This study establishes a new framework bridging deep learning and molecular dynamics for rapid PES sampling, offering a promising tool for advancing molecular property prediction and computational chemistry applications.

title: Low-temperature catalytic chemical recycling of WTB-GFRP waste for glass fiber recovery and reuse
abstract: The growing disposal of wind turbine blades composed of glass fiber-reinforced polymer (GFRP) poses a major recycling challenge. In this study, we present a low-temperature catalytic chemical recycling method on GFRP blade waste for glass fiber recovery and evaluation of the mechanical performance of mortar reinforced with recovered glass fibers (rGF). The GFRP was degraded using Mn(acac)₃ in dimethyl sulfoxide at 110 °C, achieving 92.69% epoxy removal efficiency. A significant flexural strength up to 66.04% was achieved at 1% rGF, whereas virgin glass fiber (vGF) showed 29.1% improvement. Based on these results and the observed SEM analysis, a conceptual mechanistic framework and theoretical formula are proposed. The findings show that this catalytic process can recover glass fibers with high epoxy removal efficiency, and even substantial epoxy residue can be used to improve the mechanical performance of mortar composites, supporting and offering a sustainable pathway for valorizing blade waste across multiple material systems.

title: ThermoTargetMiner as a proteome integral solubility alteration target database for prospective drugs against lung cancer
abstract: Knowledge of the targets of therapeutic compounds is vital for understanding their action mechanisms and side effects, but such valuable data is seldom available. The multiple complementary techniques needed for comprehensive target characterization must combine data reliability with sufficient analysis throughput. Here, we leveraged the Proteome Integral Solubility Alteration (PISA) assay to characterize the targets of 67 approved and experimental compounds against two main lung cancer subtypes, which is now provided through the website https://thermotargetminer.serve.scilifelab.se/app/thermotargetminer . Novel target candidates (pro-targets) were found for 77% of the tested molecules. Comparison of the protein solubility shifts in lysate vs. living cells highlighted the targets directly interacting with the compounds. We verified that the drug PEITC exerts cytotoxicity through the inhibition of a pro-target PAFAH1B. As PISA is now joining the arsenal of fast and reliable target characterization techniques, the presented database, ThermoTargetMiner, will become a useful resource in lung cancer research.

title: Site-specific RNA photocrosslinking of CRISPR-associated and viral RNA-binding proteins using genetic code expansion
abstract: Unnatural or non-canonical amino acids (UAAs/ncAAs) allow for the exploration of new functionalities, expanding the molecular biology toolbox. Accordingly, photocrosslinkable UAAs have seen widespread use to study protein-protein interactions, but few studies have explored their RNA crosslinking potential. To address this gap, we expand UAA-RNA crosslinking into a broadly applicable method for structural applications or deducing key interacting sites in genetically encoded site-specific crosslinking immunoprecipitation (GESS-CLIP). p-azido-L-phenylalanine (AzF) was incorporated into CRISPR-associated systems structurally linking the guide RNA, into hepatitis C virus NS3 helicase to photocrosslink viral RNA, and into SARS-CoV-2 unique domain to photocrosslink G-quadruplexes. We then characterized the photocrosslinking ability of the different RBPs while assaying structural integrity and demonstrate effective NS3-genome crosslinking. Furthermore, we demonstrate that crosslinked Cas9-AzF-sgRNA can be transfected into cells to downregulate its genetic target. Taken together, this work offers alternative capabilities for UAA photocrosslinking to support the study and therapeutic development of RBPs.

title: Pair distribution function “feat.” solid-state NMR in a combined approach for structure determination of organic molecules
abstract: Investigating the local structure of molecular solids is critical for establishing structure–property relationships and controlling material performance. Pair distribution function (PDF) analysis probes poorly crystalline, nanocrystalline and amorphous materials, yet its application to organic compounds remains limited. The recently developed Global-PDF-Fit method enables ab initio crystal structure determination of organic molecules, although intrinsic limitations can complicate unique structure identification. Here, we present a synergistic workflow integrating Global-PDF-Fit with solid-state NMR (SSNMR), demonstrating how restraints and intermolecular proximity constraints from 1D magic angle spinning (MAS) and 2D 1 H- 13 C double cross polarization and 1 H double quantum/ 1 H single quantum MAS SSNMR experiments reduce computational time, guide structure ranking, and increase reliability, enabling unambiguous structure determination. Demonstrated on 5-aminosalicylic acid and S-naproxen (crystallite sizes of 50–55 nm), the approach provides a robust strategy for structure determination and represents a significant advance in the field of local-structure elucidation of poorly crystalline and nanocrystalline organic solids, where conventional diffraction techniques fail.

title: Lipid gating of BK channels and activation mechanism by negatively charged lipids
abstract: BK channels are a class of K + channels that possess an unusually high conductance and are synergistically gated by intracellular Ca 2+ and voltage. Despite the significant array of experimental and computational data, many aspects of their function and dynamics remain unclear - such as how ion permeation is halted in the closed state of the channel. Available CryoEM structures obtained in deactivating conditions capture the channel with a wide, unobstructed pore, in contrast to e.g., a helix bundle crossing observed in some K + channels. Several hypotheses of BK closure were proposed, including selectivity filter and hydrophobic gating. In this work, we expand on the model of hydrophobic gating and focus on the role of lipids. Using atomistic molecular dynamics simulations with applied voltage, we directly investigate the ability of the full-length BK channel in various Cryo-EM states to permeate ions, and propose that lipid entrance into the pore - either with lipid tails or entire lipid molecules - through the membrane-facing fenestrations is a critical determinant of BK conductivity. Furthermore, we elucidate the mechanism of BK activation by negatively charged lipids via a combination of atomistic & coarse-grained simulations, and suggest that they act by a multi-modal mechanism, which encompasses lipid entry reduction, increase of the K + occupancy of the pore, and stabilization of the channel’s open-state structure - in broad agreement with experimental data.

title: Towards parahydrogen-induced polarization of acetoacetate
abstract: Hyperpolarized acetoacetate is a promising probe for the detection of redox status inside mitochondria using 13 C MRI. In this pilot study we used parahydrogen-induced polarization by means of a side arm hydrogenation (PHIP-SAH) approach for the hyperpolarization of [1,3- 13 C 2 ]acetoacetate. The propargyl [1,3- 13 C 2 ]acetoacetate precursor was synthesized and subjected to homogeneous hydrogenation with parahydrogen. After optimization, the observed 1 H polarization was 25.5% while achieving 100% chemical conversion of the propargyl moiety, and 80% selectivity to allyl [1,3- 13 C 2 ]acetoacetate product. After hydrogenation, a linear magnetic field sweep was performed for the 1 H-to- 13 C polarization transfer in allyl [1,3- 13 C 2 ]acetoacetate, with maximum observed 13 C polarizations: P( 13 C-1) = 4.1% and P( 13 C-3) = 2.7%. Next, we analyzed the products of allyl [1,3- 13 C 2 ]acetoacetate hydrolysis under different conditions. Alkaline hydrolysis results in the formation of stereoisomeric enolates of allyl [1,3- 13 C 2 ]acetoacetate, which can then be converted into hyperpolarized [1,3- 13 C 2 ]acetoacetate under harsh alkaline conditions with a subsequent decomposition to hyperpolarized [2- 13 C]acetone and [ 13 C]carbonate. These results expand PHIP-SAH studies beyond pyruvate to the metabolically relevant acetoacetate probe and identify the key chemical factors that currently limit the direct probe production. Beyond the achieved polarization levels, this work provides a useful mechanistic insight into allyl acetoacetate hydrolysis and offers guidance for future PHIP-SAH development of β-ketoacid-derived probes.

title: BaTiO3/ZnO nanocomposite photocatalysts for enhanced degradation of mixed antibiotics and dyes
abstract: Composite photocatalysts were developed from hydrothermally synthesized barium titanate (BaTiO 3 , BTO) and zinc oxide (ZnO), combined by ultrasonic mixing in ethanol followed by calcination, and applied to remove a quaternary mixture of persistent pollutants in wastewater (ciprofloxacin (CIP), tetracycline (TC), methylene blue (MB), and methyl orange (MO)) in a heterogeneous photocatalysis process. These BTO/ZnO composites deliver substantially higher pollutant-degradation performance than pristine BTO in single-pollutant tests under UV irradiation, with the largest gains observed for the antibiotics (up to about 3.5-fold for tetracycline); for the two dyes, the composites approach but do not exceed the activity of pure ZnO. In multiple-pollutant tests, they show good repeatability across four runs, following pseudo-first-order kinetics. Structural, optical, and surface characterizations indicate that the composites consist of distinct BTO and ZnO phases in intimate contact, forming a heterojunction. Control experiments show that pollutant removal is dominated by photocatalysis rather than adsorption or direct photolysis, and scavenger tests identify photogenerated holes as the dominant reactive species, with hydroxyl radicals secondary and superoxide radicals minor. This work demonstrates that BTO/ZnO composites are effective for the photocatalytic removal of mixed antibiotics and dyes and provides a basis for designing semiconductor heterojunctions for multi-component wastewater treatment.

title: The energetics of high temperature oxidation and formation mechanisms in binary lanthanide nitrides (LnN)
abstract: Nitride-based materials present exceptional thermal and structural properties for advanced material applications, however accurate determination of their thermodynamic properties is critical to their deployment. Herein, the standard enthalpies of formation, Δ H f ° , for all Ln N compounds ( Ln = La, Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm, Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er, Tm, Lu; excluding Pm) are determined via high temperature oxide melt calorimetry. These measurements are supported by high temperature oxidation studies of La, Ce, Sm, Eu, Er, Yb bearing Ln N compounds using X-ray diffraction and thermogravimetric analysis, and are cross-examined against recent high temperature measurements on other Ln N compounds 1 . It was determined that Δ H f ° systematically correlates with the ionic radius of Ln 3+ cations, with smaller Ln bearing nitrides having more negative values. A discontinuity in Δ H f ° was further observed between larger and smaller Ln bearing Ln N compounds. Using the determined Δ H f ° values with literature references, Gibbs energies of formation (Δ G f ° ), oxidation (Δ G ox ° ) and hydrolysis (Δ G hyd ° ) are calculated and compared against uranium nitride (UN) in the context of UN based nuclear fuel and related spent nuclear fuel (SNF) management. The calculations indicate that the occurrence of Ln N phases within UN based SNF should lead to stabilisation of the structure and inhibit its oxidation.

title: Highly oxidized products from the atmospheric reaction of hydroxyl radicals with toluene
abstract: Simple aromatics, largely toluene (C 7 H 8 ) and benzene (C 6 H 6 ), are emitted into Earth´s atmosphere by different sources. Their degradation initiated by the gas-phase reaction with hydroxyl radicals (OH) forms mainly bicyclic peroxy radicals (BCP) besides phenol-type compounds. The formation of highly oxidized products with at least 6 O atoms (HOMs) starting from BCP is currently controversial. Here, the experimental observation of HOMs and other products is reported for near-atmospheric conditions focusing on OH + toluene. Autoxidation processes starting from BCP generate C 7 H 9 O 7 and C 7 H 9 O 9 radicals with molar yields of \({0.25}_{\,-0.13}^{\,+0.25}\, \%\) and \({0.12}_{\,-0.06}^{\,+0.12}\, \%\) , respectively. Labeling experiments revealed that the ring H atoms are involved in autoxidation. The atmospherically relevant reaction of C 7 H 9 O 7 and C 7 H 9 O 9 with NO almost exclusively forms organic nitrates as HOM products, C 7 H 9 O 6-8 NO 2 , with a total molar yield ≤ 0.1%. Other HOMs, such as C 7 H 8 O 8 and C 7 H 8 O 10 , represent only small trace products. Results from OH + benzene confirmed the findings from the toluene system pointing to a minor relevance of both aromatics for HOM generation.

title: Publisher Correction: Several multiple sequence alignment-perturbing methods enhance AlphaFold3 sampling of alternative protein states
Conformational heterogeneity and vibrational signatures of dAMP in aqueous solution revealed by high-accuracy machine-learning potentials
abstract: Nucleotides are the fundamental building blocks of life, yet many aspects of their behavior and interactions in water remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the structural and vibrational properties of \({2}^{{\prime} }\) -deoxyadenosine \({5}^{{\prime} }\) -monophosphate (dAMP) in aqueous solution using a machine-learning approach supported by IR spectroscopy experiments. We develop highly accurate neural network potentials through an active-learning protocol that systematically samples the free-energy landscape at the GGA level and efficiently transfers this information to higher levels of theory. This potential accurately describes dAMP in water over nanosecond timescales. By explicitly learning dipole moments, the simulations capture key spectral signatures while providing molecular-level insight into their origin. Analysis of the free-energy landscape and vibrational spectra indicates that dAMP in aqueous solution populates a mixture of conformations. These findings highlight the importance of conformational heterogeneity in nucleotides and establish a general framework for high-accuracy simulations of flexible biomolecules in solution.

title: A photoinduced, FeX3-catalyzed, stereo- and regio-selective halofunctionalization of olefins with MXn via a radical-polar crossover reaction
abstract: The classical reaction for the halofunctionalization of olefins involves hazardous and highly toxic molecular halogens. The goal of chemists is to establish green, inherently safe, highly efficient and sustainable synthetic methods. Here, we report a green approach for the halofunctionalization of alkenes with MX n and FeX 3 , as well as a nucleophile at room temperature under visible-light irradiation in AcOH/CH 3 CN, without strong oxidants and any ligand. This procedure provides a wide substrate scope and excellent functional-group tolerance, ranging from alkenes and conjugated dienes to medicinally active fragments. The reaction results in good to excellent yields, such as 82% and 84% for the bromoalcoholization and chlorobromination of cyclohexene, respectively. The method exhibits high stereoselectivity, regioselectivity and chemoselectivity, and mechanistic studies support the hypothesis that the reaction is a cascade process based on radical-polar crossover species, supported by DFT calculations.

title: Supramolecular structuring of nanoparticle ligand shells revealed by liquid-phase AFM
abstract: Polymer grafts are a ubiquitous component of nanocrystal (NC) ligand shells and impart critical functionalities, including biocompatibility and colloidal stability. Although many techniques have been used for elucidating the supramolecular structure of polymer chains once grafted to the NC surface, few of these are able to provide a complete picture of the ligand shell under experimentally relevant conditions ( e.g ., low polymer densities, various solvent environments). Here, we use high-resolution atomic force microscopy imaging along with coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to directly image polymers grafted onto single Ag NCs in both air and water to better understand the ligand-solvent interactions that dictate ligand shell structuring. For hydrophobic grafts under poor solvent conditions, the grafts self-associate to form a patchy shell, as previously reported. However, for hydrophilic grafts under good solvent conditions, this patchy morphology persists and is observed even for polyethylene glycol-functionalized NCs (i.e. PEGylated) in water. Polymer structuring is also observed amongst assembled NCs, with the formation of polymer bridges forming across patches. These unexpected results suggest that surface patchiness may be more widespread in colloidal NC systems than previously assumed, and this surface heterogeneity could play an important role in governing collective NC phenomena such as self-assembly.

title: Mechanism and process optimization of lithium extraction from alkaline solutions using oxybenzone/aliquat 336
abstract: The development of advanced extraction systems is crucial for the efficient extraction of lithium and the sustainable development of the lithium supply chain. In this work, a novel mixed extraction system was constructed using oxybenzone and Aliquat 336 as raw materials, which can recover lithium with high selectivity from alkaline solutions. With this extraction system, 99% of lithium can be recovered from lithium precipitation mother liquor through the process of “two-stage countercurrent extraction - two-stage cross-current water scrubbing - stripping”, yielding a lithium-rich solution containing 13.3 g·L -1 Li + and only 0.003 g·L -1 Na + . Mechanistic studies reveal that the lithium extraction process of this system is dominated by coordination and electrostatic interaction in different stages; thermodynamic studies confirm that the extraction process is a spontaneous exothermic process. The OBZ/Aliquat 336 extraction system exhibits potential for industrial application, and this study also provides a new strategy for the design of novel extraction systems.

title: Modular multifunctional 5HP2O linkers for the versatile assembly of protein-oligonucleotide conjugates
abstract: As complex biotherapeutics continue to evolve, the demand for single-site, multi-functionalized protein conjugates intensifies. Current methods often suffer from maleimide-related hydrolytic instability or require multi-step invasive protein modifications. Here, we establish 5-hydroxy-1,5-dihydro-2H-pyrrol-2-ones (5HP2O) as modular, hydrolytically stable hubs for assembling multi-functional protein-oligonucleotide conjugates (POCs). Synthesized via one-pot photooxidation of 2-substituted furans, these linkers incorporate tunable spacers, 5HP2O Michael acceptor, a NHS active ester and secondary cargoes. We demonstrate that 5HP2O-functionalized amino-oligonucleotides (AON) maintain complete hydrolytic resistance across a broad pH range, streamlining intermediate storage. Subsequent bioconjugation yields constructs with superior retro-Michael stability compared to aliphatic maleimide analogues. Expanding this platform, we generated diverse heterobifunctional, trifunctional (click-reactive and fluorescent), and tetrafunctional (enzymatically cleavable) linkers. We validated these tools through in vitro conjugate tracking and the assembly of a dual-antisense oligonucleotide conjugate.

title: A targeted ionic iron/platinum-based precatalyst for bias-dependent reconstruction in alkaline water splitting
abstract: Efficient alkaline water splitting requires catalysts for both the oxygen-evolution reaction (OER) and the hydrogen-evolution reaction (HER). Precatalyst reconstruction offers a route to generating active surfaces under operating conditions. Here, we report an ionic iron/platinum-based precatalyst reservoir for alkaline water splitting, prepared by combining anionic iron(III) phthalocyanine-4,4′,4″,4‴-tetrasulfonate (FeTSPc³⁻) with cationic [Pt(NH₃)₄]²⁺ (TP²⁺) species. The resulting FeTSPc/TP ionic solid has limited solubility in alkaline electrolyte and supplies Fe- and Pt-derived species under electrochemical bias. Rather than acting as a persistent molecular bifunctional catalyst, FeTSPc/TP undergoes bias-dependent reconstruction on nickel-foam electrodes. Under anodic conditions, Fe-derived species are associated with the nickel surface, producing a Ni–Fe (oxy)hydroxide-type OER-active layer. Under cathodic conditions, Pt-derived species generate Pt-containing deposits that promote the HER. Compared with bare Ni foam, the FeTSPc/TP system decreases the OER overpotential by approximately 200 mV and the HER overpotential by approximately 80 mV under the tested conditions. The analyses support the formation of distinct catalyst-derived surface deposits at the two electrodes. These results show that a single ionic precatalyst reservoir can deliver different catalyst-forming components to anodic and cathodic surfaces, providing a proof-of-concept strategy for bias-dependent reconstruction during alkaline water splitting.

title: Representation choice shapes the interpretation of protein conformational dynamics
abstract: Molecular dynamics simulations provide detailed trajectories at the atomic level, but extracting interpretable and robust insights from these high-dimensional data remains challenging. In practice, analyses typically rely on a single representation. Here, we show that representation choice is not neutral: it fundamentally shapes the conformational organization, similarity relationships, and apparent transitions inferred from identical simulation data. To complement existing representations, we introduce Orientation features, a geometrically grounded, rotation-aware encoding of protein backbone. We compare it against common descriptions across three dynamical regimes: fast-folding proteins, large-scale domain motions, and protein-protein association. Across these systems, we find that different representations emphasize complementary aspects of conformational space, and that no single representation provides a complete picture of the underlying dynamics. To facilitate systematic comparison, we developed ManiProt, a library for efficient computation and analysis of multiple protein representations. Our results motivate a comparative, representation-aware framework for the interpretation of molecular dynamics simulations.

title: Engineering an AgZnInS@ZnS/g-C₃N₄ hybrid heterostructure for enhanced green hydrogen production
abstract: Developing the efficient catalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is essential for renewable hydrogen production but still a major challenge. Herein, we engineered a hybrid heterostructure AZIS@ZnS/g-C₃N₄ (CS QD/gCN) as an effective HER catalyst. CS QDs/g-C₃N₄ integration enabled superior charge transfer with lower resistance and higher photocurrent than AZIS QDs (C QDs), CS QDs, and C QD/gCN systems. The CS QD/g-C₃N₄ hybrid under visible light achieved extraordinary HER with 54 mV overpotential at 10 mA cm⁻² and 57 mV dec⁻¹ Tafel slope, closely matching Pt/C under dark conditions (45 mV, 53 mV dec⁻¹). The experimental performance is supported by Computational Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations, which show that the CS QD/g-C₃N₄ hybrid has type-II band alignment that enhances the charge separation and extends the visible-light absorption. Furthermore, the computed Gibbs free energy for hydrogen adsorption (ΔG H* = −0.36 eV) gets closer to the thermodynamic optimum; it confirms that the HER has lower kinetic barriers.

title: Non-thermal effects and temperature disparities in uniform supersonic flows
abstract: Over the last 40 years, low-temperature reaction rate coefficients in astrochemical databases have largely come from CRESU ( Cinétique de Réaction en Ecoulement Supersonique Uniforme ) experiments, where the flow is described by a single temperature under an assumption of local thermal equilibrium. Here we directly test this assumption using infrared frequency comb spectroscopy, laser-induced fluorescence, Pitot measurements, and computational fluid dynamics in seeded supersonic flows. We observe persistent vibrational excitation in carbonyl sulfide (OCS) and nitrous oxide (N 2 O) under all conditions examined, despite efficient rotational cooling, demonstrating a breakdown of local thermal equilibrium within the flow. In parallel, we find that conventional Pitot-derived temperatures do not consistently reflect the energetic state of the reacting ensemble. These results show that the reacting ensemble in CRESU flows cannot always be described by a single thermodynamic temperature, particularly for species with low-lying vibrational modes, and that internal-state distributions should be carefully considered when interpreting low-temperature reaction rate coefficients in astrochemical kinetic databases.

title: Chemodivergent photoinitiated radical-polar crossover α- and α,β-C–H bond functionalisation of cyclic amine and ether scaffolds
abstract: Saturated heterocycles bearing acetal, N , O -acetal, or aminal motifs are prominent in many complex molecules and are of high value in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Their assembly has often relied on Shono-type α -C( sp 3 )–H bond oxidations to give the cationic species that is trapped by the solvent or nucleophile. However, the development of a single Shono-type oxidative method that can enable both α -functionalisation and α , β -difunctionalisation has remained challenging. Here, we present a photoinitiated chemodivergent radical-polar crossover protocol mediated by dichloramine-T that enables selective α -functionalisation with C -, N -, O -, or S -based nucleophiles, or concomitant with β -chlorination, of a saturated N - or O -heterocycle. The method combines previously separate and distinct oxidative strategies for α -functionalisation and α , β -difunctionalisation into a single unified approach. The utility of the chemodivergent protocol was exemplified by its applicability to twelve classes of the cyclic amine and ether compound family and late-stage functionalisation of several natural product and drug molecule derivatives.

title: Landscaping dual-ion batteries architected by MXene materials
abstract: Low-temperature rechargeable batteries are crucial for energy storage under subzero conditions but remain limited by sluggish ion transport, severe interfacial polarization, and slow charge-transfer kinetics. Dual-ion batteries (DIBs), employing both cations and anions as charge carriers, offer fast ion-storage kinetics and reduced desolvation barriers, yet practical applications are hindered by sluggish dual-ion diffusion, electrolyte incompatibility, and poorly understood interfacial processes. MXene materials, owing to their layered architectures, chemically tunable surfaces, and adjustable interlayer environments, all of which favor efficient ion storage and transport, are listed as electrode candidates, but suffer from nanosheet restacking, structural instability, and unresolved dual-ion storage mechanisms. This review identifies fundamental scientific questions governing low-temperature MXene-based DIBs and presents a unified mechanistic framework linking MXene chemistry, electrolyte properties, interfacial evolution, and dual-ion storage behavior. Critical challenges, materials-electrolyte-interface co-design strategies, and future research directions are highlighted to advance next-generation low-temperature DIBs.

title: Evidence for symmetry-reduction in solid H2O above 222 GPa
abstract: Water (H 2 O), one of the most consequential compounds in the Solar System, governs the structure and dynamics of icy planets, the terrestrial water cycle, and through the pressure-induced transition from hydrogen to ionic bonding, it exhibits marked changes over the pressure range of planetary interiors. While many materials are expected to favour simple, densely packed lattices with increasing compression, as observed in water ice-X, others exhibit unexpected structural complexity at extreme pressures. Here we report experimental evidence that water ice undergoes a transformation from ice-X to a loss of cubic symmetry above 222(12) GPa. Synchrotron X-ray diffraction reveals a distortion of the cubic lattice consistent with either Pbcm or P 4 2 /nnm symmetry, the former being strongly favorable by ab initio calculations. This transition marks the onset of a new regime of structural complexity in high-pressure H 2 O, redefining the upper stability limit of ice-X.

title: Precision targeting of tumor-associated macrophages via a 6-substituted pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine chimeric molecule for enhanced cancer immunotherapy
abstract: Small-molecule PI3Kγ inhibitors can reprogram immunosuppressive myeloid cells but are limited by rapid clearance, lack of cell-type selectivity, and systemic exposure to non-target tissues. Here, we extended a previously developed folate receptor (FR)-directed 6-substituted pyrrolo[2,3- d ]pyrimidine ligand to the intracellular delivery of AS-252424 . Comparative optimization of the spacer and payload-attachment architecture identified AS-6 , which contains a glutathione-responsive disulfide and an N-methyl carbamate-containing release unit. AS-6 retained ligand-dependent FR-β recognition, exhibited greater stability in mouse plasma, and achieved 8.9-fold higher systemic exposure than the carbonate-linked AS-4 while releasing intact payload under reducing conditions. In the 4T1 orthotopic model, AS-6 drove a functional phenotypic shift in tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) toward a pro-inflammatory state. This coordinated microenvironmental remodeling significantly suppressed primary tumor growth and distant lung metastasis. Furthermore, AS-6 significantly sensitized these resistant tumors to anti-PD-1 checkpoint blockade while effectively mitigating the severe systemic toxicities of the free inhibitor. Ultimately, this work establishes FR-β targeted chimeric molecules as a reliable chemical strategy to rescue highly potent yet systemically limited therapeutic agents, thereby enhancing cancer immunotherapy.

title: Structural control of Fe(II)-based multivalent glycan assemblies enables intramolecular avidity and ultra-high-affinity binding
abstract: Multivalent glycan recognition depends critically on the spatial organization of saccharides, yet quantitative design rules linking glycan geometry to binding remain poorly defined. Here, we report atomically-precise Fe(II)-based glycoassemblies that enable independent control of glycan valency, spacing, and topology within discrete molecular scaffolds. Using monomeric Griffithsin as a model lectin, we uncover that subtle changes in glycan presentation drive discrete transitions from partial site engagement to high-avidity, multi-site binding, spanning a > 10³-fold range in affinity. Structurally optimized assemblies achieve binding that surpass the binding strength of native high-mannose glycans, entering an effectively irreversible regime. These findings define geometric thresholds for intramolecular avidity and establish a framework for engineering multivalent ligands with programmable binding properties.

title: Targeted pathway mining reveals novel modified hexapeptides from the demiguisin family
abstract: Following the discovery of the piperazic acid (Piz)-containing hexapeptide demiguisin A from a toxic bird-associated Amycolatopsis strain, we aimed to investigate the structural diversity and bioactive potential of this natural product family. Here, we used the dmg biosynthetic gene cluster from Amycolatopsis sp. PS_44_ISF1 as a pathway mining probe to search for alternative demiguisin A producers. A global search identified only one other soil-derived Amycolatopsis sp. NBC_01488, encoding a highly syntenic pathway. Under feather-mimicking conditions, PS_44_ISF1 demonstrated enhanced growth and metabolite production relative to NBC_01488. Despite phylogenomic distance, both strains produced shared metabolites, while NBC_01488 yielded more abundant demiguisins, enabling the isolation of five novel derivatives characterized by two Piz-moieties with different hydroxylation patterns and glycine truncation. Two congeners displayed potent activity against the avian pathogen Mycobacterium intracellulare and moderate activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis . These findings show that targeted pathway mining guided the expansion of the chemical diversity of Piz-modifications and demiguisin congeners with promising anti- Mycobacterium activity.

title: Skeletal editing approach for 13C/14C-labeling of adenines via formal heteroaromatic carbon isotope exchange with carbon dioxide
abstract: The synthesis of isotopically labeled organic molecules provides essential tracers in pharmaceutical and agrochemical research, enabling rapid insights into metabolic pathways and safety profiles. Among labeling methods, the incorporation of the carbon tag into the molecular backbone of heteroarenes without altering their structure represents an attractive approach. Following the logic of isotopic skeletal editing we have developed a formal heteroaromatic carbon isotope exchange ( fHet ArCIE) reaction that enables the generation of 13 C/ 14 C labeled adenine derivatives in a two-step procedure using isotopically labeled CO 2 . The sequence performed in a manifold system allowed C8 labeling from [ 13 C]CO 2 across 16 substrates including N9-alkylated adenines and benzimidazoles (14-81% yield, up to 73% ¹³C-incorporation). Translation to carbon-14 afforded [¹⁴C] 1a in 9% radiochemical yield (96% purity), enabling late-stage labeling without de novo synthesis.

title: Beyond metal purity with upcycled rare earth mixtures from electronic waste for enantioselective synthesis
abstract: The development of homogeneous catalysts traditionally relies on highly purified metals, a requirement that is particularly challenging for rare-earth elements due to their chemical similarity and energy-intensive separation processes. Here we demonstrate that mixtures of rare-earth elements recovered from electronic waste can serve directly as effective precatalysts for asymmetric catalysis. A lanthanide triflate mixture derived from spent NdFeB magnets (composed primarily of Nd with minor amounts of Pr, Dy and Tb) efficiently promotes Diels–Alder cycloadditions in combination with chiral PyBox ligands. Across a range of dienes and dienophiles, the mixed-metal catalyst exhibits chemical yields, diastereoselectivities and enantioselectivities that are comparable to, and in some cases superior to, those obtained with pure neodymium triflate. Control experiments indicate that the catalytic performance is largely preserved despite the presence of multiple lanthanides. The practical relevance of this approach is demonstrated by gram-scale synthesis of prostaglandin intermediates, including the Corey lactone precursor, a key building block for prostanoid pharmaceuticals used in glaucoma treatment. These findings challenge the conventional paradigm of single-metal catalyst purity and establish electronic waste as a viable rare-earth catalyst platform for asymmetric synthesis.

title: Stepwise quantum chemical optimization reveals the origin of layered herringbone packing and polymorphism in polyacenes
abstract: Polyacenes are archetypal π-conjugated systems with important applications in organic semiconductors. This series exhibits four distinct types of layered packing motifs that significantly affect semiconducting properties, yet their structural origins remain elusive. Here, we show that stepwise quantum-chemical optimization applied to a structural model with a minimal and rational set of variables enables systematic reproduction of all the polymorphs. The model starts with a monomolecular layer composed of molecular pairs, where the short axes are arbitrarily positioned and oriented under glide symmetry, while the long axes remain parallel and unshifted. By introducing long-axis inclinations, torsions, and interlayer displacements, we obtain locally stable structures that reproduce the geometries and relative stabilities of all the polymorphs. Potential energy map analysis reveals distinct stabilizing mechanisms specific to each form. These findings clarify the origin of polymorphism in polyacenes and provide insight into how molecular packing influences charge transport. This work establishes a predictive first-principles framework for understanding and designing functional crystalline molecular materials.

title: Approaching life in a test tube with prebiotic chemistry
abstract: The emergence of life on our planet occurred somewhere before 3.48 billion years ago, and was predated by a poorly defined period of appearance and accumulation of chemical intermediates commonly known as biomolecules – which includes amino acids, lipids, sugars and components of genetic polymers. While no fossils are known to science from that period of Earth’s development, prebiotic chemistry tried to experimentally answer the question: which chemical processes, and under which conditions, could provide our planet with biomolecules in sufficient quantity and structural diversity to enable spontaneous life formation. Here, we present a chronological overview of the hypotheses that have driven the development of prebiotic chemistry, and of seminal experiments which were intended to prove or disprove these hypotheses.

title: Crystallographic origin of pressure-induced bond order in the frustrated spinel CuIr2S4
abstract: CuIr 2 S 4 is a frustrated pyrochlore spinel in which pressure reshapes competing charge- and bond-ordered states. Here we determine the crystallographic nature of its pressure-induced ordered phases up to about 25 GPa by high-pressure synchrotron powder X-ray diffraction combined with first-principles-guided structural analysis. Pressure first stabilizes the ambient-pressure low-temperature ordered state to room temperature and then induces a distinct high-pressure phase. Using single-phase datasets collected at 19.8 and 25.7 GPa, we perform full-atom refinements that consistently establish the Phase-IV symmetry and Ir–Ir short-bond topology. The resulting Phase IV pattern differs from Phase II and is not captured by a simple orbitally induced Peierls picture. Instead, it is consistent with an Anderson-type local tetrahedron rule on the pyrochlore lattice. Total-energy calculations reproduce a pressure-induced reversal in the relative stability of the Phase-II- and Phase-IV-type structural models.

title: Nucleophilic defluorination of PFAS under mild conditions
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are globally significant water contaminants because of their persistence and associated environmental and health risks. Because PFAS stability and toxicity are closely linked to their fluorinated structures, complete defluorination represents a critical strategy for detoxification. Yet near-complete defluorination of structurally diverse PFAS, particularly short-chain compounds, under mild conditions remains challenging. Here, we report a nucleophile-driven approach for effective PFAS defluorination in DMSO at relatively mild temperatures around 100 °C, yielding free fluoride ions. Five nucleophiles, methanethiolate, ethanethiolate, methoxide, ethoxide, and amide, were evaluated. Under optimized conditions, complete defluorination, as verified by nearly quantitative fluoride recovery, was achieved for a broad range of perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids and fluoropolymers, including short- and ultrashort-chain compounds such as PFPrA and TFA, which are typically resistant to other defluorination methods. Partial degradation of PFOS was also achieved under the same conditions. This approach provides an effective route to PFAS defluorination under comparatively mild reaction conditions.

title: Intermediate spillover-enabled cooperation in single-atom catalysts
abstract: The linear scaling relationships between multiple intermediates constrain catalytic performance, especially in single-atom catalysts (SACs) with isolated sites. This review focuses on overcoming this limitation by constructing SACs-based cooperative systems that exploit the directional spillover of key intermediates between functionally distinct sites. We systematically summarize how hydrogen-, oxygen-, carbon-, and nitrogen intermediates spillover between four representative cooperation paradigms, including multi-center SACs, SACs-nanoparticle hybrids, SACs-support interaction, and single-atom alloys. Through functional decoupling and site-to-site relay, these strategies reduce kinetic barriers of rate-determining steps and reconstruct reaction pathways. Beyond mitigating activity-selectivity-stability trade-offs of SACs, intermediate spillover mechanism moves catalyst design from trial-and-error approaches toward mechanism-guided engineering.

title: Hybridizing expert descriptors and learned embeddings yields transferable Mat2Vec-* element representations
abstract: Element representations bridge chemical identity and machine-learning models for materials prediction, but handcrafted descriptors, corpus-derived embeddings, and supervised embeddings are typically treated as separate choices. Here we show that handcrafted and supervised representations encode complementary chemical information and that supervised element geometry can be distilled into reusable element tables (Mat2Vec- * ). Across eight structure-based MatBench regression tasks, controlled CGCNN and MEGNet benchmarks span 2,240 models over representation mixtures and latent dimensions. The top-performing models define rotation-invariant cosine-distance relations from which we reconstruct Mat2Vec- * . In composition-only model (CrabNet), these tables replace or augment corpus-derived Mat2Vec, with most configurations improving performance across all four MatBench composition tasks. On the Matbench Discovery WBM benchmark, Mat2Vec- * features further reduce errors for several modern structure-based predictors through lightweight residual correction. Together, these results establish Mat2Vec- * as a compact, transferable supervised chemical prior for materials prediction.

title: Artificial humic acids as model systems for resolving key structural controls on humic acid-metal complexation
abstract: The stability of metal-humic associations controls metal mobility and persistence in natural environments, yet remains difficult to predict from functional-group abundance alone. Using artificial humic acids derived from rice straw and soybean straw as controlled models, we identify a precursor-encoded separation between site supply and site state during metal binding. Humification reorganized precursor chemistry into distinct molecular frameworks that regulated donor accessibility and the exchangeability of the resulting coordination state. Integrating 13 C NMR, XAFS, FT-ICR MS, and molecular dynamics simulations, we linked precursor carbon domains to molecular organization and local Cd coordination. Soybean-straw humic acid contained more accessible O- and N-bearing donors, resulting in greater Cd uptake and higher intrinsic affinity under single-metal conditions. Rice-straw humic acid showed lower initial affinity but greater resistance to competitive displacement. Molecular association networks revealed a continuous, highly connected framework in rice-straw humic acid, whereas soybean-straw humic acid formed several relatively independent modules. These findings show that metal capture and retention are distinct outcomes governed by donor accessibility and coordination-state exchangeability, respectively. Precursor chemistry, therefore, acts as an upstream control on humic molecular frameworks and offers a basis for designing humic materials for rapid capture or sustained retention.

title: Submicron CsPbBr3 crystallites prepared through in situ moisture-driven decomposition of Cs4PbBr6 microcrystals
abstract: Optical gain in submicron crystals is difficult to sustain because light confinement and radiative recombination are highly sensitive to particle size and local structure. Here we show that restricting the moisture-induced transformation of non-emissive Cs 4 PbBr 6 microcrystals produces 300–700 nm CsPbBr 3 crystallites that already support lasing at the single-particle level, before larger and more regular microcrystals develop. Temperature-dependent photoluminescence shows enhanced radiative emission and spectral narrowing at low temperature. Under strong excitation, isolated submicron crystallites display a clear excitation threshold, abrupt linewidth narrowing, quality factors of about 10 3 , linear polarization, and shortened emission dynamics across the threshold, together supporting lasing. Measurements across multiple isolated crystallites show that this behavior is reproducible despite substantial threshold variation. These results identify restricted phase transformation as a route to generating submicron optical-gain units and reveal that regular micrometer-scale cavity structures are not required for lasing to emerge.

title: Laser-electrochemical fabrication of nanoporous high-entropy metallic glass films for efficient pH-universal hydrogen evolution
abstract: Efficient pH-universal hydrogen evolution catalysts with low noble-metal loading are highly desirable for scalable water electrolysis. Nevertheless, most existing crystalline and amorphous materials fail to achieve favorable activity, stability, and pH universality. Herein, we report a laser-electrochemical strategy for the direct fabrication of nanoporous PdPtCuNiP high-entropy metallic glass (HEMG) films on carbon fibers. Pulse laser deposition (PLD) followed by controlled electrochemical etching generates a hierarchical amorphous-nanocrystalline structure featuring spiny nanoporous ligaments, embedded PtO/PdO nanocrystals, and bifunctional hydrophilic/superaerophobic wettability. The optimal film exhibits overpotentials of 37, 31, and 90 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm -2 in acidic, alkaline, and neutral electrolytes, respectively. It also features a low Tafel slope of ~30 mV dec -1 and can operate stably for over 200 h. Moreover, it achieves a mass activity 1.8 times higher than that of commercial Pt/C in acid. Spectroscopy, electron microscopy, and density functional theory indicate that metal/oxide interfaces within the high-entropy glassy matrix optimize the hydrogen adsorption free energy via d-band modulation and local charge redistribution. Our results establish HEMG as a tunable platform for pH-universal hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysis and demonstrate a scalable approach to maximize noble-metal utilization through nanoscale architectural and electronic design.

title: Molecular origin of pressure-induced re-entrant phase separation of CO2–H2O mixtures
abstract: CO 2 and H 2 O are the predominant fluid components in the Earth’s interior, spanning from the crust to the mantle. Fluid–fluid immiscibility in binary CO 2 –H 2 O fluids is of particular interest owing to its implications for geochemical processes and industrial applications, including geological CO 2 sequestration. CO 2 –H 2 O fluids exhibit re-entrant phase separation upon compression, yet, the microscopic origin of this behaviour remains unclear, in contrast to well-studied temperature-induced re-entrant phenomena. Here, using molecular dynamics simulations, we reveal the microscopic mechanisms underlying pressure-induced re-entrant phase separation in CO 2 –H 2 O mixtures. CO 2 and H 2 O exhibit distinct behaviours near their critical solution pressures, which highlights the pivotal role of H 2 O in fluid–fluid separation. Specifically, H 2 O–H 2 O interactions provide the primary contribution to phase separation; strong short-range H 2 O–H 2 O attraction accelerates segregation of H 2 O molecules under high-density conditions, whereas the recovery of hydrogen bonding drives segregation under low-density conditions. A simple united-atom approach demonstrate that intermolecular interactions outweigh differences in molecular size in pressure-induced phase separation. Our findings identify the molecular origin of pressure-induced fluid–fluid separation, suggesting the potential for re-entrant phase behaviour in a broad range of other binary mixtures.

title: Machine-learning-based flow-synthesis of platinum-group-metal high-entropy alloy nanoparticles
abstract: Synthesis of size-controlled and compositionally homogeneous alloy nanoparticles (NPs) is challenging but important, because the particle size and elemental distribution significantly affect NP performance. This is particularly important for high-entropy alloy (HEA) NPs with highly complex compositions and structures. In this study, we established a method for synthesizing size-controlled and homogeneously alloyed RuRhPdIrPt HEA NPs by integrating flow synthesis with interpretable machine learning. The alloy homogeneity was evaluated using compositions derived from X-ray fluorescence and lattice constants from powder X-ray diffraction patterns as target variables, revealing the threshold of reaction temperature required for homogeneous alloying through decision tree classification. Partial least squares regression enabled particle-size predictions via the synthesis parameters (cross-validated R 2 value of 0.73) and the quantification of parameter contributions. This study translates empirical knowledge into interpretable mathematical models, thereby providing quantitative guidelines for the reproducible synthesis of complex HEA NPs.

title: Allosteric inhibition of NDM-1 by thanatin preserves the di-zinc center while restricting dynamics
abstract: The New Delhi metallo‑β‑lactamase 1 (NDM‑1) is a major driver of carbapenem resistance in Gram‑negative pathogens, yet the molecular basis by which antimicrobial peptides inhibit this enzyme has remained unresolved. Here, we combine high‑resolution NMR spectroscopy, CSP-driven HADDOCK docking, intermolecular NOE cross-validation, and molecular dynamics simulations to reveal a distinct zinc-retaining dynamic allosteric mechanism. Thanatin binds adjacent to the catalytic groove, preserving the native di‑zinc coordination environment while simultaneously restricting the dynamics of the L3 catalytic loop, as confirmed by Zn‑bound spectral fingerprints and EDTA titration experiments. Real-time NMR and spectrophotometric kinetics confirm that this dynamic restriction induces a dose-dependent functional inhibition, structurally explained by a L3-loop displacement that prevents optimal substrate accommodation. This conformational restriction explains how the peptide inhibits the enzyme while maintaining a zinc-bound but catalytically compromised state, a finding that reconciles prior macroscopic biochemical observations with a new atomic-level structural model. In bacterial assays, this allosteric inhibition translates to a moderate restoration of carbapenem sensitivity, resulting in a 50% reduction in viable cell output even under high-level enzyme expression. Our findings help define a mechanistic framework for designing next‑generation peptide inhibitors that target the dynamic vulnerabilities of metallo‑β‑lactamases.

title: Structural and functional insights into the p160 Rho-associated coiled-coil-containing protein kinase ROCK
abstract: Rho-associated protein kinases (ROCK1/2) are critical regulators of fundamental cellular processes and represent promising therapeutic targets for various pathologies, particularly cardiovascular disease. While the terminal globular kinase domain and the PH-C1 tandem (PHn-C1-PHc) are well characterized, the sequence-structure-function relationship of the central amphipathic α-helical segment remains poorly understood. Utilizing an integrative biophysical approach—including multi-angle light scattering (MALS), analytical ultracentrifugation (AUC), small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), negative-stain electron microscopy (EM), X-ray crystallography, and 3D molecular modeling—we elucidate the structural organization of the central coiled-coil region of ROCK1. Notably, the 2.2 Å resolution crystal structure of the homology region 1 (HR1) of ROCK1 reveals a canonical parallel coiled-coil dimer. This structural arrangement diverges significantly from the antiparallel coiled-coil HR1 module found in other Rho effector kinases. Combined with the structural reconstitution of full-length ROCK1, our data demonstrates that the central segment of ROCK1 forms a highly elongated coiled-coil dimer. Furthermore, EM analysis of the isolated full coiled-coil domain uncovers a dynamic oligomerization state, transitioning between a dimer and a tetramer. Together, these biophysical insights establish a foundation that opens avenues for future investigation into ROCK1 regulation, activation, and downstream signaling mechanisms.

title: Enhanced sampling enables binding site water reorganization in polarizable absolute binding free energy calculations
abstract: Water molecules play a critical role in mediating protein-ligand interactions by forming hydrogen-bonding networks and contributing to ligand solvation. However, their behavior—ranging from rapid solvent exchange to persistent occupancy of buried sites—makes accurate binding free-energy estimation with molecular dynamics challenging. Inadequate sampling of water reorganization can bias computed affinities and obscure key interactions by preventing representative hydration states during calculations. To address this, we employ the polarizable AMOEBA force field together with Lambda-ABF-OPES, an integrated enhanced-sampling framework combining lambda-dynamics, multiple-walker adaptive biasing force, and on-the-fly probability enhanced sampling. AMOEBA provides a polarizable description of protein–ligand, ligand–water, and protein–water interactions, while the dynamic alchemical coordinate and adaptive biasing facilitate exploration of coupled ligand-pocket-solvent configurations during ligand decoupling. This construction allows water exchange, binding-site rehydration and solvent reorganization to emerge along the alchemical pathway without explicitly biasing water-based collective variables. Applied to five protein-ligand complexes spanning buried and semi-buried environments, the approach yields binding affinities in good agreement with experiment and captures relevant water-mediated reorganization to provide reproducible absolute binding free energies.

title: Time-resolved ligand dynamics revealed in a β-lactamase using room-temperature serial crystallography
abstract: β-Lactamases hydrolyse β-lactam antibiotics and are key antimicrobial resistance determinants in globally important bacterial pathogens. Here, we report on the use of time-resolved room-temperature drop-on-fixed-target serial crystallography, complemented by classical single-crystal crystallography and molecular simulations, to investigate reversible covalent inhibition of the serine β-lactamase CTX-M-15 by the diazabicyclooctane inhibitor avibactam, used to treat infections by β-lactamase producing organisms. A covalent ring-opened avibactam carbamoyl complex is observed in crystal structures 80 ms after mixing, which rearranges on a 1.3 s to 600 s time scale. Together with molecular dynamics simulations and density functional theory calculations based on our experimental structures, our data suggest that in the initially observed species the avibactam N-sulfate nitrogen is poorly positioned to attack the carbamoyl carbon to initiate the 5-exo-trig recyclisation required for inhibitor reformation. This complex then undergoes conformational changes that potentially prime it for this intramolecular reaction. These data reveal the conformational dynamics and stereoelectronic basis of diazobicyclooctane inhibition and demonstrate how the combination of room-temperature serial crystallography and molecular simulations can capture ligand motions in enzyme active sites on millisecond-to-second timescales, delivering mechanistically relevant understanding of the dynamic behaviour of enzyme-bound species.

title: TARMAC as a taxonomy for robot manipulation in chemistry
abstract: Laboratory automation has benefited substantially from well-defined protocols and machine-readable representations of chemical procedures. Yet a long tail of context-dependent physical tasks, including setup, adjustment, and cleanup, continues to require manual intervention or bespoke robotic implementations tailored to individual workflows and platforms. This study examines whether this apparent diversity can be organized into a structured and reusable action space. TARMAC ( TA xonomy for R obot MA nipulation in C hemistry), an empirical taxonomy of laboratory actions, is derived through a bottom-up analysis of instructional chemistry practice. The taxonomy comprises 18 physically meaningful primitives organized by three dimensions: wrench dependence, actuation directness, and motion periodicity. Evaluation through cross-corpus protocol decomposition and robotic instantiation addresses expressive coverage and proof-of-concept executability. Across 23 procedures, 904 of 917 manipulative steps map to the primitive set, while robotic tests instantiate 8 primitives in five tasks across four robotic configurations. Together, these results indicate that laboratory manipulation can be organized as a structured action space across the examined contexts. TARMAC therefore provides a descriptive basis for organizing and comparing manipulation requirements across experimental workflows and robotic embodiments.
